Chi-squared tests for categorical features

Source: R/fs_chi.R
fs_chi.Rd

Tests each categorical feature for association with a categorical target using the chi-squared test of independence, adjusts the p-values for multiple testing, and keeps the features whose adjusted p-value is below sig_level.

Usage

fs_chi(
  data,
  target,
  sig_level = 0.05,
  continuity_correction = NULL,
  p_adjust_method = "bonferroni",
  simulation_B = 2000,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE,
  n_cores = 2L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or data.table holding the features and the target. Column names must be unique, non-empty, and not NA. The input object is never modified.

target

Name of the target column. It is converted to a factor if necessary and must have at least 2 levels among its non-missing values.

sig_level

Significance threshold for the adjusted p-values, strictly between 0 and 1. Default 0.05.

continuity_correction

NULL, TRUE, or FALSE. Controls Yates' correction for 2x2 tables tested asymptotically. NULL (the default) and TRUE both apply it; FALSE turns it off. Tables larger than 2x2 and simulated p-values are never corrected.

p_adjust_method

Multiple-testing correction, one of stats::p.adjust.methods, matched case-insensitively. Default "bonferroni"; "none" turns correction off. An invalid name is an error before any feature is tested. Only tested features count toward the correction: a skipped feature keeps an NA adjusted p-value and does not raise the multiplier for the others. With k tested and s skipped features, "bonferroni" multiplies by k, not k + s.

simulation_B

Number of Monte Carlo replicates for the simulated p-value used when any expected cell count is below 5. A whole number of at least 100; default 2000. A simulated p-value is never below 1 / (simulation_B + 1), so after adjustment it may be unable to reach sig_level at all. With Bonferroni this happens once the number of tested features reaches sig_level * (simulation_B + 1), which is 101 at the defaults. A warning then names the affected features and the simulation_B you would need.

seed

Optional integer. When supplied, the RNG is seeded for this call and the previous RNG state is restored on exit, which makes simulated p-values reproducible. With parallel = TRUE the simulations draw from furrr's parallel-safe streams instead (furrr_options(seed = TRUE)), so a given seed gives reproducible parallel results that differ from the sequential ones. Default NULL (featR does not touch the RNG).

verbose

If TRUE, report target conversion, skipped features, and the worker count. Default FALSE.

parallel

If TRUE, test features in parallel using the suggested furrr and future packages. Default FALSE.

n_cores

Number of workers when parallel = TRUE, a whole number of at least 1, capped at the detected core count. Default 2. If the current future plan is sequential (the future default), featR sets a future::multisession plan with this many workers for the duration of the call and restores the previous plan on exit, even if worker start-up fails. If you have already set a non-sequential plan, for example future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4), featR uses it as is, leaves its workers running, and ignores n_cores.

Value

An fs_result object with:

selected

Features with an adjusted p-value below sig_level.

scores

Named numeric vector of adjusted p-values, one per candidate factor feature, NA for skipped features. Smaller means stronger evidence of association, the opposite of most featR scores.

method

"chi".

task

"classification".

model

NULL; no model is fitted.

details

A list with results, sig_level, p_adjust_method (as supplied), and n_features (the number of candidate factor features, skipped ones included). results is a data frame with one row per candidate feature, ordered by adjusted then raw p-value with skipped features last. Its columns are:

  • feature: the column name.

  • n: for tested features, the number of complete feature-target pairs; for skipped features, the feature's count of non-missing values.

  • df: degrees of freedom; NA for simulated and skipped tests.

  • p_value, adj_p_value: raw and adjusted p-values.

  • significant: TRUE when adj_p_value < sig_level, so FALSE for skipped features.

  • method: "asymptotic" or "simulation"; NA when skipped.

  • correction_applied: whether Yates' correction was actually applied. A 2x2 table whose counts equal their expected values gets no correction even when one was requested. NA when skipped.

  • min_expected: the smallest expected cell count; NA when skipped.

call

The matched call.

Details

For each feature, the test asks whether the feature and the target are distributed jointly the way independence would predict. Features are tested one at a time, so the result describes marginal association only. A feature that matters only in combination with another is missed, and two features carrying the same information are both reported as significant.

A p-value measures evidence against independence and says nothing about the size of the effect. With enough rows a negligible association still clears any sig_level.

Which columns are tested

Character columns are converted to factors, and then every factor column other than the target is tested. Numeric, logical, and date columns are ignored, so convert or discretize them first if you want them tested. If no factor features remain, the result has an empty selection and no error is raised. A numeric target is converted with as.factor(), so each distinct value becomes its own class.

Missing values and sparse tables

Each feature is tested on its own complete cases (rows where both the feature and the target are observed), so n can differ between features. Levels left empty after that filtering are dropped. If the feature or the target then has fewer than two levels, the feature is skipped: it gets an NA p-value and is not selected.

A feature is tested with the asymptotic chi-squared statistic when every expected cell count is at least 5. Otherwise the p-value comes from a Monte Carlo simulation with simulation_B replicates. A simulated p-value changes from run to run unless seed is set, and its df is NA. Yates' continuity correction applies only to 2x2 tables on the asymptotic path, whatever continuity_correction says.

See also

The Filter methods guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  f1 = factor(rep(c("A", "B", "A"), times = c(40, 40, 20))),
  f2 = factor(rep(c("X", "Y"), times = 50)),
  target = factor(rep(c("Yes", "No"), each = 50))
)
out <- fs_chi(d, "target")
out$selected
#> [1] "f1"
out$details$results
#>   feature   n df      p_value  adj_p_value significant     method
#> 1      f1 100  1 0.0001051636 0.0002103271        TRUE asymptotic
#> 2      f2 100  1 1.0000000000 1.0000000000       FALSE asymptotic
#>   correction_applied min_expected
#> 1               TRUE           20
#> 2              FALSE           25
